title: Semilinear functoriality of the two-sided bar augmentation roof
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal D$ be a small ordinary category, $R$ a commutative ring, $F:\mathcal D\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ a covariant functor, and $Q:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal D$ a simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For $p,q\geq0$ put
$$A_{p,q}=\bigoplus_{T_0\to\cdots\to T_p\xrightarrow f Q_q}F(T_0).$$
Horizontal faces delete $T_i$, applying $F(T_0\to T_1)$ when $i=0$ and composing with $f$ when $i=p$; vertical operators postcompose $f$ with the operators of $Q$. Let $\partial_h,\partial_v$ be the alternating face sums in positive respective indices, zero at index zero. Put $A_{p,q}$ in cochain bidegree $(-p,-q)$ and use finite-diagonal total differential $\partial_h+(-1)^p\partial_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Put $S^{-q}=F(Q_q)$ with alternating-face differential and zero positive terms. Put $B^{-p}=\bigoplus_{T_0\to\cdots\to T_p}F(T_0)$, zero in positive degrees, with alternating faces deleting $T_i$ and applying $F$ only at the first face. Complexes and their derived categories mean [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal D',R',F',Q',A',S',B',e'_Q,e'_B$ be defined by the same formulas with primed data; $e_Q$ is zero for $p>0$ and sends $(T\xrightarrow fQ_q,x)$ to $F(f)x$, and $e_B$ is zero for $q>0$ and forgets $f$ on $q=0$, with the same definitions for the primed maps. Let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ be a functor, $\rho:R\to R'$ a ring map, $\theta:F\to\operatorname{Res}_\rho(F'\circ u)$ a natural transformation, and $k:uQ\to Q'$ a simplicial morphism. Then
$$(T_0\to\cdots\to T_p\xrightarrow fQ_q,x)\longmapsto(uT_0\to\cdots\to uT_p\xrightarrow{k_q u(f)}Q'_q,\theta_{T_0}x)$$
defines a morphism of commuting double complexes and hence a total chain map $V:\operatorname{Tot}A\to\operatorname{Res}_\rho\operatorname{Tot}A'$. Define $t:S\to\operatorname{Res}_\rho S'$ by $t^{-q}=F'(k_q)\theta_{Q_q}$ and $b:B\to\operatorname{Res}_\rho B'$ by $(T_0\to\cdots\to T_p,x)\mapsto(uT_0\to\cdots\to uT_p,\theta_{T_0}x)$. They are chain maps and satisfy
$$e'_QV=t e_Q,\qquad e'_BV=b e_B$$
after restriction of scalars. These constructions preserve identities and composition, with the usual identifications of iterated restriction of scalars. Degreewise restriction preserves direct sums, kernels, images and quasi-isomorphisms, identifies the displayed total and edge complexes with their restrictions, and takes inverses of localized quasi-isomorphisms to their inverses. Thus these two strict squares remain the same squares in $D(R)$. No representable contractibility assumption on $Q,Q'$ or $uQ$ is needed for these assertions. The formula for $V$ and both strict squares involve no choice of contracting homotopies.

source.place: Tags 08PH (example-morphism-categories), 08PD (remark-morphism-fibred-categories), and 08Q9 (lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution). Agent-written strict two-sided-bar version, including semilinear coefficients and degreewise scalar restriction.

proof.text: Write $\operatorname{Res}_\rho M$ for the same abelian group as $M$, with $r x=\rho(r)x$, and restrict maps by retaining their underlying functions. The direct sum of modules is the group of finite-support tuples with coordinatewise scalar action, so the identity on tuples gives $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Res}_\rho M_i\cong\operatorname{Res}_\rho(\bigoplus_iM_i)$, including empty sums. Kernels and images are the same subsets before and after restriction; cokernels are the same quotient groups with the restricted action. Finite products also have the same coordinatewise action. Thus restriction is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits: products and kernels of differences describe the former, finite sums and cokernels describe the latter. In particular restriction is exact. All indexing sets here are small, since the category is small and strings have finite length.

proof.text: First check that the displayed differentials define commuting double complexes. Horizontal faces obey $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ for $i<j$: deleting distinct internal vertices amounts to composing the same arrows in either order; at the first vertex this is $F(ba)=F(b)F(a)$, and at the last vertex it is associativity of the composite with $f$. Vertical faces obey the same relations because $Q$ is a functor on $\Delta^{op}$. For either alternating differential, the two occurrences corresponding to $i<j$ have signs $(-1)^{i+j}$ and $(-1)^{i+j-1}$, so they cancel; at degrees zero and one its square is zero by the zero outgoing differential at index zero. Horizontal deletion commutes with postcomposition of $f$: at the last vertex both orders give $Q(\alpha)fa$, at the first vertex postcomposition does not change the coefficient map. Hence $\partial_h\partial_v=\partial_v\partial_h$, as required by the commuting convention. The identical argument gives the complexes $S,B$ and all primed complexes.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), generator formula; agent-written two-sided semilinear refinement

proof.text: Each summand map defining $V_{p,q}$ is $R$-linear into the restricted target: $\theta_T(rx)=\rho(r)\theta_T(x)$. It extends uniquely by finite sums even when different strings acquire the same image. For a horizontal first face $a:T_0\to T_1$, the two coefficient values agree by $\theta_{T_1}F(a)=F'(u(a))\theta_{T_0}$. Internal faces commute with $u$ because $u(ba)=u(b)u(a)$. For the last face with $a:T_{p-1}\to T_p$, both final arrows are $k_q u(f)u(a)=k_q u(fa)$. Thus $V$ commutes with every horizontal face, and hence with $\partial_h$; at $p=0$ both horizontal differentials are zero.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), generator formula; agent-written two-sided semilinear refinement

proof.text: For every simplicial operator $\alpha$ taking degree $q$ to $r$, the morphism condition on $k$ is $Q'(\alpha)k_q=k_r u(Q(\alpha))$. Postcomposing with $u(f)$ proves that $V$ commutes with that operator, including degeneracies; its coefficient stays $\theta_{T_0}x$. Thus $V\partial_v=\partial'_vV$. On the summand in total degree $-p-q$, $V$ preserves $p$, so it commutes with the sign $(-1)^p$ as well. The finite sum of the $V_{p,q}$ therefore commutes with $\partial_h+(-1)^p\partial_v$. The total differential squares to zero: its mixed terms have coefficients $(-1)^{p-1}$ and $(-1)^p$, which cancel, and its two unmixed squares vanish by step 2. Each diagonal has $p+q=-n$ and only $-n+1$ possible pairs when $n\leq0$, so the total is defined without an infinite diagonal sum.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), generator formula; agent-written two-sided semilinear refinement

proof.text:
For a face $d_i:Q_q\to Q_{q-1}$, naturality of $\theta$ followed by naturality of $k$ gives
$$F'(d'_i)F'(k_q)\theta_{Q_q}=F'(k_{q-1})F'(u(d_i))\theta_{Q_q}=F'(k_{q-1})\theta_{Q_{q-1}}F(d_i).$$
Taking alternating sums proves that $t$ is a chain map (outgoing differentials at degree zero are zero). For $b$, the first face commutes by $F'(u(a))\theta_{T_0}=\theta_{T_1}F(a)$, and every other face commutes by functoriality of $u$; summing proves that $b$ is a chain map. Both maps are $R$-linear by the same coefficient calculation as in step 3.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), generator formula; agent-written two-sided semilinear refinement

proof.text: The edge maps themselves are chain maps. For $e_Q$, on the $p=0$ edge the vertical differential is unsigned and commutes with evaluation because $F(Q(\alpha)f)=F(Q(\alpha))F(f)$. The only horizontal contribution entering that edge comes from $p=1$: its two evaluations are $F(f)F(a)x$ and $F(fa)x$, equal and with opposite signs. At $p>1$ both evaluations are zero. For $e_B$, on the $q=0$ edge forgetting $f$ commutes with every horizontal face. The only vertical contribution entering that edge is from $q=1$, where forgetting either $d_0f$ or $d_1f$ gives the same string and coefficient; their difference, even multiplied by $(-1)^p$, is zero. At $q>1$ both composites vanish. The primed edge maps satisfy the same checks.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), generator formula; agent-written two-sided semilinear refinement

proof.text:
Check the two strict squares on each summand. On $p=0$ the evaluation square is the identity
$$F'(k_q u(f))\theta_Tx=F'(k_q)\theta_{Q_q}F(f)x,$$
by naturality of $\theta$ for $f:T\to Q_q$. On $p>0$ both sides vanish, since $V$ preserves $p$. On $q=0$ the forgetful square sends a generator on either path to $(uT_0\to\cdots\to uT_p,\theta_{T_0}x)$; on $q>0$ both sides vanish. Equality on summands gives $e'_QV=t e_Q$ and $e'_BV=b e_B$ as chain-map equalities. These calculations use neither contractibility nor contracting homotopies.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), generator formula; agent-written two-sided semilinear refinement

proof.text:
For second data $(v,\sigma,\psi,l)$ with $l:vQ'\to Q''$, the composite data are $(vu,\sigma\rho,\chi,m)$ with $\chi_T=\psi_{uT}\theta_T$ and $m_q=l_qv(k_q)$. Composing the two $V$ formulas sends a generator to the string $vuT_0\to\cdots\to vuT_p$ ending by $l_qv(k_q)vu(f)$ and coefficient $\psi_{uT_0}\theta_{T_0}x$, exactly the formula for the composite data. The same coefficient equality proves composition for $b$. For $t$, naturality of $\psi$ for $k_q$ gives
$$F''(l_q)\psi_{Q'_q}F'(k_q)\theta_{Q_q}=F''(l_qv(k_q))\psi_{uQ_q}\theta_{Q_q}.$$
For identity data the formulas fix every string and coefficient. Restricting successively along $\sigma$ then $\rho$ gives $r x=\sigma(\rho(r))x$, the action for $\sigma\rho$; all identity and composition equalities are therefore under the stated iterated restriction identification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to $\operatorname{Res}_\rho:\operatorname{Mod}_{R'}\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$, additive and preserving finite limits and finite colimits by step 1. It supplies preservation of quasi-isomorphisms and the functor $D(R')\to D(R)$ represented on every complex by degreewise restriction, together with its natural localization comparison. By step 1 the direct sums defining $A',B'$ are identified by the identity on finite-support tuples with their restricted versions; $S'$ is identified degreewise in the same way. Their face maps retain the same underlying functions and the total sign is unchanged. Finite diagonal sums thus give the identical restriction comparison for $\operatorname{Tot}A'$. In particular the strict squares of step 7 have precisely the displayed objects and maps after restriction and localization.

source.place: Tags 08PD/08PH, change-of-category maps; derived passage supplied by derived.tex, Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor)

proof.text:
Let $s$ be any quasi-isomorphism of primed complexes. Its localized image is invertible, and functoriality gives
$$\operatorname{Res}_\rho(Q'(s)^{-1})\operatorname{Res}_\rho(Q'(s))=1=\operatorname{Res}_\rho(Q'(s))\operatorname{Res}_\rho(Q'(s)^{-1}).$$
Consequently the image of the inverse is the inverse of the image, under the natural localization comparison of step 9. Applying the localization functor to the equal composites in each strict square preserves those equalities. Applying it also to step 8 preserves identities and composition. This proves all derived assertions, without asserting that either edge augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism for arbitrary $Q$.
